attack_story.title: Linux Digital Detective Investigation
narrative: Repeated SSH authentication failures were detected from 192.0.2.50 against account(s) admin, root. This behavior is consistent with credential-guessing activity.
A successful SSH authentication occurred after the failed authentication sequence. This materially increases the likelihood that the targeted account was successfully accessed.
The authentication sequence was followed by an SSH session, providing additional evidence of successful account access.

A privilege transition was detected through sudo execution. This indicates that the authenticated account obtained higher local privileges and requires investigation. Observed command(s): /usr/bin/id; /usr/bin/cat /etc/shadow; /usr/bin/apt-get update; /usr/bin/systemctl status ssh; /bin/bash.
Credential-access behavior was observed, indicating possible attempts to obtain or inspect authentication material.
Network reconnaissance activity was detected, indicating possible enumeration of services, network configuration, or active connections.
Persistence-related activity was detected, suggesting a possible attempt to maintain access beyond the initial session.
Remote content transfer or command-and-control behavior was observed.
attack_story.conclusion: The available evidence is consistent with an SSH-based compromise involving repeated authentication failures, subsequent successful authentication, and a later privilege transition to a higher-privileged account. Observed user=admin, root and source=192.0.2.50. Overall assessed risk is CRITICAL (100/100).
